questions.question: From which ancient Greek words does the word "democracy" derive?
questions.explanation: "Democracy" comes from demos (people) and kratos (power or rule), meaning "rule by the people".

questions.question: What does the principle of "popular sovereignty" mean?
options: Government authority derives from the consent of the governed
questions.explanation: Popular sovereignty means the government derives its authority from the consent of the governed, who choose their leaders through elections.

questions.question: Which principle is captured by the idea "one person, one vote"?
questions.explanation: Political equality means every citizen has an equal right to participate, reflected in "one person, one vote".

questions.question: Which form of democracy was practised in ancient Athens?
questions.explanation: Ancient Athens practised direct democracy, where citizens voted on laws themselves, though it excluded large parts of the population.

questions.question: Which condition must elections meet to be genuinely democratic?
options: They must be free, fair, transparent and periodic
They must be held only once
They must be decided by judges
questions.explanation: Genuinely democratic elections must be free, fair, transparent and periodic to ensure real accountability.
